body: Worker rule (Termal::BarA2, 2026-10-28 17:27Z, from my own slip while preparing a B16 slice; refined by Fable2 #760). Never run a shell command with another session's worktree as the working directory, and that includes read-only ones like `sed`, `cat` or `git status`. A command from another writable session in a worktree can refuse the credit of a run there, and git status can even refresh the index. To read someone else's root, use the Read and Grep tools, which run no commands. If a git command is truly needed, run it as `git -C <root>` from my own working directory, and never while that root has a live run. If a command does land there, tell the coordinator and that session at once, naming the commands and their times.
